insights.statement: The €3.0M a year claim is 12% of the full €25M spend, but €1.1M of that spend is rush freight that no unit-price cut touches, so the gross price lever is €2.87M a year
insights.decision_relevance: Sets the correct gross base for every option

insights.statement: Rush freight is our problem, not the supplier's: €0.65M of the €1.1M falls in five months flagged as our forecast errors, so it survives any supplier choice
insights.decision_relevance: Separate forecasting lever outside this decision; not counted in any option

insights.statement: If Supplier B's last two stoppages recur, they cost €4.0M over 2026-2028 at full exposure, 46% of the €8.6M three-year gross saving of full consolidation
insights.decision_relevance: The risk is the largest cost in the case and must be charged to every option

insights.statement: Costed on the same three components (price, switching, stoppage risk by Supplier B share), full consolidation nets €3.8M over three years, against €2.08M for a 70/30 split and a net cost of €1.2M for the status quo
insights.decision_relevance: Ranks the options: consolidation still wins on expected value

insights.statement: Full consolidation stays ahead of a 70/30 split unless three-year stoppage cost exceeds €9.76M, 2.4x history; but it leaves no second source, and the incumbent can cover 60% of volume only at two weeks' notice
insights.decision_relevance: The choice is robust on expected value; the residual exposure is a tail risk to contract away
insights.caveat: H6 unresolved: whether a standby agreement with the incumbent is obtainable

insights.statement: The real saving of full consolidation is €1.27M a year (€3.8M over three years), not €3.0M a year (€9.0M): €5.2M of the claimed saving will not materialise
insights.decision_relevance: The budget must book 3.804 EUR M over 2026-2028, not 9.0
